title: A screen can show the column grid you are designing to
goal: Real UI is laid out on columns: twelve columns with a gutter, or a four column phone layout. Photonz can arrange things in a stack or a grid container, but there is no way to put a column guide behind a whole screen and see whether the pieces on it land on the columns. This puts an optional column overlay on a screen, set by its number of columns, its gutter and its margin.
notes: BLOCKED on its decision card until the user answers, because it puts something new on screen. From the ui-grid mock, and named as unbuilt in the rough list of queue/audits/2026-09-03-auto-layout.json: the mock layout grid is a column overlay you eyeball against, not a container that positions what it holds, and only the container was built. Ships behind next-frames since only a screen carries one, or its own Next flag if the runner prefers; either way on by default in Next. The overlay is chrome, not content: it belongs with the canvas overlays in CanvasView, not in the render path, so it can never reach an export. Whether it also snaps is the card question, and the answer decides whether LayerSnapping is touched at all.
acceptance: A screen can be given a column overlay with a column count, a gutter and a margin, all typed
The columns draw behind everything on that screen, at every zoom, and never appear in an export or a copied picture
The overlay can be switched off and on for a screen without losing its numbers
Each screen keeps its own settings, and a document with none of them is byte for byte what it was
Try it with Build on a frame turned on in Experiments: draw a screen, set twelve columns, and drop two boxes onto it
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task
